source_text:
εὐηγγελίσω μοι, φησίν, πῶς δυνατὸν εἶναι τὸν Χριστὸν ἐκ Ναζαρέθ, ὃν εἶπεν ἡ
γραφὴ ἐκ Βηθλέεμ ἔρχεσθαι; ἀλλ' ἐκεῖ μὲν ἐν Βηθλέεμ ἐτέχθη, τὴν δὲ Ναζαρὲθ
ἐπεγράφετο πατρίδα ὡς ἐκεῖ τραφεὶς καὶ διάγων μέχρι τελείας ἡλικίας. 51 {3Jο 1,
47}3Μεγάλη δόξα καὶ καύχημα τὸ ἐξ αὐτῆς τῆς ἀληθείας, ὅ ἐστι Χριστός, μαρτυρίαν
ἔχειν καθαρᾶς καρδίας, ἥτις ὁρᾷ θεὸν τῷ νῷ καὶ ποδηγεῖται πρὸς τὴν σωτήριον
πίστιν ἀδόλως προστρέχειν τῷ Χριστῷ οὐχ ὡς Ἰουδαῖος ἢ ὡς Ἡρώδης. 52 {3Jο 1,
49}3Ὅλος ἕτοιμος ἦν ὁ Ναθαναήλ. διὸ ἐκ μόνου τούτου τοῦ ψιλοῦ ῥήματος πεισθεὶς
ὡμολόγησεν αὐτὸν εἶναι τὸν Χριστόν, ὅς ἐστιν υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ φύσει καὶ ἀληθείᾳ καὶ
βασιλεὺς τῶν ὄντως πιστῶν· ὡς ἔτι γὰρ ἀτελὴς οὐκ εἶπεν αὐτὸν βασιλέα τῆς
κτίσεως, ἀλλὰ μόνον τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον· «καὶ ἐγενήθη μερὶς κυρίου
λαὸς αὐτοῦ Ἰακώβ, σχοίνισμα κληρονομίας αὐτοῦ Ἰσραήλ». 53 {3Jο 1, 51}3Ὁτὲ μὲν
ἁπλῶς, ὁτὲ δὲ διπλασιαζομένως κέχρηται ὁ σωτὴρ τὸ βέβαιον τῶν λεγομένων
παριστάς. ἔστι δὲ ἡ λέξις ἑβραϊκὴ δηλοῦσα τὸ γένοιτο οὕτως ὑμᾶς πιστοὺς εὑρεθῆναι
ὡς ἰδεῖν τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀνεῳγότα καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. οὐκ αἰσθητῶς δέ, φησίν, τὸν οὐρανὸν
ἀνεῳγότα δυνατὸν ἰδεῖν, ἀλλὰ μόνον νοήσει σκοπούσῃ τοὺς προσερχομένους
ἀγγέλους ἐπὶ τῷ διακονεῖν τῷ Ἰησοῦ. ἔστι δὲ τὸ ἀμὴν καὶ ἀντὶ τοῦ ὄντως καὶ ἀληθῶς
λεγόμενον, ὃ καὶ κρεῖττον ἐνταῦθα. 54 {3Jο 1, 51}3Ἐπειδὴ μόνου τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ
ὠνόμασεν ὁ Ναθαναὴλ τὸν Χριστὸν βασιλέα, παιδεύει αὐτὸν διὰ τούτου, ὅτι οὐκ ἦν
ψιλὸς ἄνθρωπος ὁ Χριστός, ἐπεί πως αὐτῷ ὑπηρετοῦσιν ἄγγελοι. 55 {3Jο 1,
51}3∆είκνυσι διὰ τούτου, ὅτι οὐ δοκήσει, ἀλλ' ἀληθείᾳ γέγονεν ἄνθρωπος. ἐκΜαρίας
σαρκωθεὶς ὡς μόνος ἀναμάρτητος ὢν ἔσῳζεν αὐτῷ τὸ «κατ' εἰκόνα» ὅπερ πρῶτος
ἄνθρωπος εἶχεν ὁ «κατ' εἰκόνα καὶ καθ' ὁμοίωσιν» θεοῦ γεγονώς. 56 {3Jο 2, 2}3
56Ἦλθεν ὁ κύριος εἰς τὸν γάμον, ἵν' ἁγιάσῃ οὐ μόνον τοὺς ζῶντας, ἀλλὰ καὶ τοὺς
μέλλοντας τεχθῆναι, δεικνύς, ὅτι αὐτὸς ἐξ ἀρχῆς τὸν γάμον ἐθέσπισεν δεδωκὼς τῷ
Ἀδὰμ τὴν Εὔαν, καί τινας τῶν αἱρετικῶν καταισχύνῃ τῶν δια βαλλόντων τὸν γάμον.
57 {3Jο 2, 4}3Τῇ δὲ μητρὶ ἐπιμέμφεται ὡς ἀκαίρως ὑπομνησάσῃ θεὸν ὑπ
pass_a_gloss: Glory is witness from truth—Christ—of a pure heart that sees God by mind and runs to saving faith without Jewish or Herodian guile. Nathanael was ready; one bare word made him confess Christ as natural true Son of God and king of true believers; as still incomplete he said king of Israel only, per Deuteronomy’s portion language. Amen is sometimes single, sometimes doubled for firmness; Hebrew ‘so be it’ that they be found faithful to see opened heaven—by mind watching serving angels, not sense. Amen also means truly. Naming Christ Israel’s king alone, he teaches Christ is not bare man because angels serve him. Not doketic: truly man from Mary, sinless, keeping the image Adam had. He came to the wedding to sanctify living and unborn, affirming marriage from Adam and Eve against heretics who slander marriage. He rebukes Mary’s untimely reminder: do not take me for mere man; manifestation time has not come. Untimely push toward wonder-working is rebuked. Metretes equals 150 xestai. He who waters vines into wine now turns water to wine. Some call Cana first of all signs; others first among signs but not absolute first. Signs open a faith door revealing glory and power. He expelled law-sacrifices to bring spiritual worship. Father is his own as sole natural offspring. God’s house is merchandise of spiritual goods, not belly-bound fleshly trade.
pass_b_english: Great glory and boast it is to have from the truth itself—that is Christ—witness of a pure heart, which sees God with the mind and is led toward saving faith to run to Christ without guile, not as a Jew or as Herod.

Nathanael was wholly ready. Therefore persuaded from this bare saying alone he confessed him to be the Christ, who is Son of God by nature and truth and king of the truly faithful; for still incomplete he did not call him king of creation, but only of Israel according to what was said: “And the Lord’s portion became his people Jacob, the measured inheritance of his inheritance Israel” (Deuteronomy 32:9).

Sometimes simply, sometimes doubled, the Savior uses “Amen,” presenting the firmness of what is said. The word is Hebrew, declaring “so be it” that you be found faithful so as to see heaven opened and what follows. Not sensibly, he says, is it possible to see heaven opened, but only by mind that watches the angels approaching to serve Jesus. “Amen” is also said for “truly and really,” which is better here.
Since Nathanael named Christ king of Israel alone, he teaches him through this that Christ was not a bare man, since somehow angels serve him.

He shows through this that not by appearance but in truth he became man. Incarnate from Mary as alone sinless he preserved for himself the “according to the image” which the first man had who came to be “according to the image and according to likeness” of God (Genesis 1:26).

The Lord came to the wedding that he might sanctify not only those living but also those about to be born, showing that he from the beginning ordained marriage, having given Eve to Adam, and that he might put to shame certain heretics who slander marriage.

He rebukes the mother for untimely reminding a God who needs no reminder—as if to say, do not think me to be only man, but also God. The time of my manifestation has not yet come; it is not yet known who I am.
He rebukes the mother for urging him toward wonder-working out of season.
The metretes makes one hundred fifty xestai.
He who by water waters the vine and makes it bear wine is himself the one who also now changes the water into wine.
Some say this the first sign in Cana, but not first of all. Some indeed say the wedding in Cana the first sign, but first of all.
He opened them a door of faith through the divine signs, revealing himself—that is, his glory and power.
He cast out the things sacrificed according to law, that he might bring in spiritual worship in their place.
Christ calls God his own Father as himself alone existing from him according to nature.
The house of God is a house of merchandise, but not of these fleshly things that go “into the belly,” but of spiritual goods.
